# Tests: blockers of visible blocked items are pinned (selection + grouping)

## Goal

As a test author, I want the blocker-pinning contract pinned by tests BEFORE the implementation lands, so that the implementation (children 2 and 3 of WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC) is driven by failing tests that reproduce the reported defect and each acceptance criterion, exactly as the AC coverage review and test-first ordering require.

Discovered from: WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC (Herdr selection list blocker invisibility).

## Summary

Write the failing test surface that defines the blocker-pinning behaviour end-to-end: the §Reproduction selection shape against a seeded real worklog DB (AC1), the grouping pin semantics (AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC9), the three parent-substitution cases (AC6), the shared-`isActiveBlocker` terminal cases (AC7), the spawn-count guard (AC8) and the dispatch-head ordering (AC10). These tests target `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and the fetcher worklist-bundle pipeline and must FAIL (red) before the implementation children land and turn green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (tests) — Blocker visibility reproduction test.** `fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` adds a test reproducing the §Reproduction shape exactly (20 root completed/in_review items, 4 blocked roots, open root blockers, `browseItemCount` = 20) against a **seeded real worklog DB** (the `seedSubstitutionDb` pattern in that file, `WorklogDatabase` from `@worklog/shared`), and asserts **each root blocker id is selected** — not merely "not dropped by the count window". The test is red before the implementation child lands.
- **AC2/AC3/AC4 (tests) — grouping pin semantics.** `grouping.test.ts` adds tests asserting: a pinned blocker carries the *same* `group` and `groupLabel` as the blocked item despite having no shared key files (AC2); when a blocker blocks two visible blocked items in different groups it appears exactly once, in the **first (lowest-numbered) group** in display order (AC2); within the group the pinned blocker is placed **immediately after** the blocked item it was pinned for (AC3); the selected list contains **no duplicate ids** and **no item visible today becomes invisible** (AC4). Red before the grouping child lands.
- **AC5 (tests) — no-op regression.** `grouping.test.ts` (and, if cheap, the bundle test) asserts that when no visible item has an active blocker, the selected list and its grouping are **byte-identical to today's output** over a fixture with no blocked items.
- **AC6 (tests) — three parent-substitution cases.** `fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` adds the three required cases: (a) child blocker under a third-party parent → the ROOT is pinned and the child id never appears at top level; (b) child blocker whose root IS the blocked item (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` / `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` shape) → no row added at all, no duplicate, child reachable via expand of the parent; (c) nested child blocker → the TOP-MOST ancestor is pinned (mirroring the existing nested-critical-child test). Also assert **no leftover `parentId` item appears in the selected list** (generalisation of the root-only assertion), and that the existing critical-child substitution tests still pass unchanged.
- **AC7 (tests) — one active-blocker predicate.** A test (in `fetcher-blockers.test.ts` or the pin tests) covers each terminal case of the shared `isActiveBlocker` predicate used for pinning: `completed`/`deleted` status targets and targets at stage `in_review`/`done` are **not** pinned.
- **AC8 (tests) — read cost.** `fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` / split-guard suites stay green; a pinned selection adds **no new `wl` process spawn per visible blocked item** on the default path (the pin read reuses the batched in-process `fetchOutboundDepsForItems` read or the consolidated bundle).
- **AC9 (tests) — content determinism.** A test shuffles the input item order (same item set + same dependency edges) and asserts **identical pinned grouping** (same group numbers), so group assignment stays a pure function of content + edges, never of arrival order.
- **AC10 (tests) — dispatch head.** A test (index/downtime-worker level) asserts `getHerdrListHead` output changes deliberately with pinning: pinned blockers become candidates from the same selection the dispatcher ranks, so the ordering change is deliberate rather than incidental.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-blockers.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` (assertion fixture only — no behaviour change in this item)

## Deliverables

- Red tests for every criterion above, following the repo's vitest conventions and the existing `seedSubstitutionDb`/mock-`wl` fixture patterns.
- A comment on the parent recording which tests were added and that they fail before the implementation children land.
